findings.reason: The protected source is a concise finite-state cycle solution: it greedily matches one source block, recognizes repeated target positions at block boundaries, and skips the resulting periodic behavior. Its state and counter names express genuine algorithmic concepts, so no inert candidate is justified.

At most |s2| boundary positions are discovered and revisited, each after scanning |s1| characters, which supports O(|s1| · |s2|) time and O(|s2|) state; the lowercase-only alphabet sets are constant-sized.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064957484. It is algorithmically identical to the protected source in alphabet rejection, target-position advancement, completed-copy counting, initial boundary state, cycle deltas, whole-cycle jump, map clearing, leftover simulation, and final division; only the LeetCode class wrapper differs.

The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.00x the reference runtime. A correct direct-scan control passed every opaque correctness execution and every benchmark output but failed only the runtime verdict at 129.76x.

The Approach now corresponds exactly to the protected target. It explains the alphabet prerequisite, greedy cross-block matching, sufficiency of the boundary position, cycle-delta calculation, map clearing after the jump, final grouping by n2, and the stated bounds using string lengths rather than the invalid former abs(s2) wording.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement.
